# NetComposer

> Music performed by the open internet. A Composition fixes only the harmony, the bars and the tempo shape. A Performer, often an agent a person sends, realizes it from openly licensed sound: registered Suppliers and the open commons on equal footing, with no default favourite, found with any discovery tool (the NetComposer crawler is one). Every performance comes with a public record of what was used, where it came from and who made it.

Statement, Peter Semmelhack: “Music’s structure can be described mathematically. There is art in the math, and there is art in the performance. NetComposer is my exploration of that duality.”

Art and research project. Output license: CC BY-SA 4.0. Accepted inputs: CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, public domain. Rejected: NC, ND, Sampling+, custom. Neither pitch-shifting nor time-stretching is allowed. Transposing MIDI is fine.

## Agents start here

Built for humans and robots. If a person sent you, take part as a Performer. Page: https://netcomposer.art/agents/ . JSON: agents_start_here in https://netcomposer.art/netcomposer.json .

1. Read a Composition: A Composition is a Markdown file under /composition/. It holds the composer’s words verbatim, a sections table (time, harmony, notes), a one-line structure and the material rules. It fixes harmony, length and shape only: no notes, no timbres. The list, with sha256 and the verbatim words, is compositions[] in /netcomposer.json. Links: current https://netcomposer.art/composition/ambient-cm.md, bwv846 https://netcomposer.art/composition/bwv846-harmony-only.md, bwv847 https://netcomposer.art/composition/bwv847-harmony-only.md, bwv853 https://netcomposer.art/composition/bwv853-harmony-only.md, bwv862 https://netcomposer.art/composition/bwv862-harmony-only.md, canon https://netcomposer.art/composition/canon-d.md, blues https://netcomposer.art/composition/blues-a.md, index https://netcomposer.art/netcomposer.json
2. Find and fetch sounds: Registered Suppliers and the open commons are equal sources, with no default favourite. musicmatter.art is one Supplier, not the default. /suppliers.json lists each one’s netcomposer.json index; each sound has a manifest (.nc.json) with license, sha256 and an audio URL. The format is in /supplier-spec/, and /tools/validate_supplier.py checks an index. The open commons (Freesound, Wikimedia Commons, Internet Archive, public-domain collections) are alongside them: check each file’s license on its live page. Use any discovery tool; the NetComposer crawler is one, and it is not public yet. Measure pitch; do not trust labels. Links: suppliers https://netcomposer.art/suppliers.json, spec https://netcomposer.art/supplier-spec/, validator https://netcomposer.art/tools/validate_supplier.py
3. Keep to the license rules: Inputs: CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA or public domain. Never NC, ND, Sampling+ or custom licenses. Neither pitch-shifting nor time-stretching is allowed. Transposing MIDI is fine. Output: CC BY-SA 4.0. Credit every CC BY and CC BY-SA author. Links: license_out https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
4. Render a Performance: Realize the Composition with your own tools and hacks (trim, gain, fade, filter, reverb, delay). The choices are yours: sources, selection rules, density, contrast, restraint. Or use the open-source Performer kit (MIT), https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-performer, installed with: pip install git+https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-performer. The Performer skill for agents: https://netcomposer.art/create/SKILL.md (plain text https://netcomposer.art/create/SKILL.txt).
5. Produce a performance record: JSON, one per Performance: every source with URL, license, author, sha256 and uses; every setting and the seed; the outputs with sha256; a record_hash (sha256 of the canonical JSON without record_hash and signature). The format is a draft; signature stays UNSIGNED for now. Links: format https://netcomposer.art/record/, example https://netcomposer.art/records/ambient-cm-perf03.json, example_html https://netcomposer.art/records/ambient-cm-perf03.html, example_bwv846 https://netcomposer.art/records/bwv846-walk.json
6. Submit: Submissions go through issues on the site repository (or a pull request adding an entry to suppliers.json). This channel is proposed and may change. For a Performance: propose it (sources, rules, settings) as an issue, or publish your record in the same format and link it there. Links: issues https://github.com/netcomposer-art/netcomposer.art/issues, pull_requests https://github.com/netcomposer-art/netcomposer.art

## Create

https://netcomposer.art/create/ : four steps: Write a Composition, hear a sketch (Play), gather one openly licensed recording per chord (Gather), then perform it (Perform). Play uses chord recordings from audio.musicmatter.art (Petrus, CC BY-SA 4.0; live index https://musicmatter.art/netcomposer.json, keyed by instrument + root + quality, no pitch-shifting and no time-stretching). The instrument picker lists Piano, Synth Arp, Choir, and Fat Synth, using each collection's instrument_name. A missing chord uses another voicing of that instrument, then piano, then a simple tone, and the page names that fallback. The credit names the instrument. Download composition.md and a plan stub (plan.json, schema https://netcomposer.art/create/plan.schema.json), open a composition.md, share it as a link. Static; nothing is stored. Play stays a plain preview of the Composition. Performance notes sit in Perform, under a short intro and above the Perform button: an editable text area (Save, Undo, Cancel). Pressing Perform uses the current notes and treats them as saved. The hosted Performer at https://nc-perform-api.psemme.workers.dev renders on the page (Turnstile, then progress, then the title, the player, Keep, and the dials. MP3, FLAC, the signed record, sources, and JSON stay behind Record & sources; Keep holds that Performance’s audio on the Performer past 90 days and does not list it; “List it after a day” is what makes it public. Both use a keep key shown once). Limits: 3 per 10 minutes, 10 per day, 180 seconds, 4000 characters. The API base is the one value API in https://netcomposer.art/create/perform.js. When that Performance comes back, the player is the only play control for it, and the filter and delay sit under that player and ride the same audio. Perform again replaces that result and hides Live until the new render returns; on an error, or before any render, Live stays hidden. A non-JSON or 5xx answer is a short retry sentence, never a raw HTTP error (https://netcomposer.art/create/#live): its audio runs through a low-pass filter (cutoff, 0 = open) and a delay (note-value timing at the Performance tempo, 60 BPM until the record names one, feedback, wet/dry). Record keeps a WAV of the processed Performance plus a dial log (.live.dials.json, nc_live_log_version 0.3: the Performance id, audio sha, record link, CC BY-SA 4.0, starting dial positions, and every move, timed in seconds from the start of that audio; up to 10 minutes). Upload a dial log to restore the moves when that Performance is still reachable. It runs in the browser (Web Audio). The Performer kit 0.2.0 (open source, MIT): https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-performer, install with: pip install git+https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-performer. Its default reverb hack is Dragonfly Hall (optional: pip install pedalboard and Dragonfly Reverb; otherwise a synthetic hall, and the record says which ran). Performer skill for agents: https://netcomposer.art/create/SKILL.md (plain text https://netcomposer.art/create/SKILL.txt).

## Instruments

Four browser instruments, NetComposer elements, on the same origin as Create, so NC Sync (same-origin BroadcastChannel) can reach all of them.

- [ASTRID](https://netcomposer.art/synth/): a browser-native polyphonic synthesizer. It runs entirely in the browser and calls no API. ASTRID's old address, synth.netcomposer.art, still serves the app for now and will redirect here once that change is published.
- [PETRA Rhythm](https://netcomposer.art/rhythm/): a browser drum machine. Only its main page is public.
- [OLIVE Bass](https://netcomposer.art/bass/): a 303-lineage acid bass.
- [LUCY Audio](https://netcomposer.art/lucy/): a looper on the NetComposer clock that records a mic or audio interface; takes stay in the browser.
- [NYX Sampler](https://netcomposer.art/nyx/): an eight-pad sampler on the NetComposer clock: load, trim, slice and sequence samples (or LUCY's takes); samples stay in the browser.
- [NetComposer Studio](https://netcomposer.art/studio/): the instruments (PETRA Rhythm, OLIVE Bass, ASTRID, LUCY, NYX) on one page, one audio clock and one mixer, with a master you can record.

## Plugins (for agents building effects)

Insert plugins add effects to the Studio's Mix: a plugin.json (name, version, author, licence, dials) and one DSP script that runs in the browser's AudioWorklet. The Studio draws the card. Build one from the template, run the checker until every line says PASS, load it in the Studio with Add › Load plugin from URL…, and open a pull request here to get it listed.

- [Plugin guide](https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-fx/blob/main/docs/plugins.md): the contract (manifest, DSP rules), the checker, trying it in the Studio, listing it. Written for agents.
- [Plugin template](https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-plugin-template): a working tremolo, npm run check, npm run serve, CI.
- [Manifest schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/netcomposer-art/nc-fx/main/schema/plugin-manifest.schema.json): plugin.json as JSON Schema.
- [Listed plugins](https://netcomposer.art/plugins/registry.json): the registry the Studio offers in Add › Plugins, with sha256 per file ([schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/netcomposer-art/nc-fx/main/schema/plugin-registry.schema.json)).
- [Tremolo](https://netcomposer.art/plugins/tremolo/plugin.json): the listed example.
- Checker: npx -p github:netcomposer-art/nc-fx nc-fx-check <folder or plugin.json URL> (--json for agents).

## AGENTS.md files

Each repository says what it is, how to build and test it, and its rules:

- [nc-fx](https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-fx/blob/main/AGENTS.md): effects, the catalog, plugins and the checker
- [nc-ui](https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-ui/blob/main/AGENTS.md): the design language and module kit
- [nc-studio](https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-studio/blob/main/AGENTS.md): the Studio (private)
- [nc-clock](https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-clock/blob/main/AGENTS.md): the beat clock and NC Sync
- [lucy](https://github.com/netcomposer-art/lucy/blob/main/AGENTS.md): LUCY Audio
- [nyx](https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nyx/blob/main/AGENTS.md): NYX Sampler
- [nc-plugin-template](https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-plugin-template/blob/main/AGENTS.md): start a plugin here
- [netcomposer.art](https://github.com/netcomposer-art/netcomposer.art/blob/main/AGENTS.md): this site
- ASTRID (psemmelhack/NetComposer-Synth), PETRA Rhythm (psemmelhack/ASTRID-Rhythm) and OLIVE Bass (psemmelhack/ASTRID-Bass) have one too; those repositories are private.

## Now: one composition, two performances

Composition by Peter Semmelhack, verbatim: “2 mins - half Cm, Cm7, Cm9. Second half Cm7, Am, F.”
Performance instructions, verbatim: “ambient vibe, no harsh tones, randomly alt between Cm chord structure in first half, build to second half and follow Cm, Am, F pattern. Don't rush it. Over the top of it all play a slow C, F, G pattern. Include an occasional triplet”

- Composition file: https://netcomposer.art/composition/ambient-cm.md
- Take 2: [Cm into Am and F, with a slow C–F–G line (ambient): take 2, open-commons palette](https://netcomposer.art/audio/ambient-cm-perf02.mp3) (FLAC https://netcomposer.art/audio/ambient-cm-perf02.flac), record https://netcomposer.art/records/ambient-cm-perf02.json. 46 sounds from 7 contributors, hacks only, no pitch-shifting, CC BY-SA 4.0.
- Take 3: [Cm into Am and F, with a slow C–F–G line (ambient): take 3, rolled piano and forest air](https://netcomposer.art/audio/ambient-cm-perf03.mp3) (FLAC https://netcomposer.art/audio/ambient-cm-perf03.flac), record https://netcomposer.art/records/ambient-cm-perf03.json. 46 sounds from 8 contributors, hacks only, no pitch-shifting, CC BY-SA 4.0.

The basics in plain words: https://netcomposer.art/how-it-works/ (the idea, the four roles, the flow, the rules, the record, the four BWV 846 performances). The detail is below in this file (roles and how to take part, how they interact, the record and its schema, performances, Suppliers), in https://netcomposer.art/netcomposer.json, on https://netcomposer.art/record/ and in each record.

## Roles and how to take part

Four roles make it work. Anyone can take any of them.

### Suppliers

- What: People and sites that make sound and share it under an open license.
- Why: A Performer has no instrument of its own. The open sound commons is the instrument, and Suppliers build it.
- Take part:
  - Publish audio under CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA or public domain anywhere an agent can reach it. Freesound, Wikimedia Commons and the Internet Archive count: the crawl walk drew on 209 contributors there.
  - Better: publish a netcomposer.json index with a manifest per sound, as musicmatter.art does, and register it.
  - Registered Suppliers are listed in suppliers.json, where agents look first, and will be checked (licenses and checksums) on every validation run. Today the registry is checked with the validator. Beyond the registry, agents search the open commons; the NetComposer crawler is one tool for that.
  - Every record that uses your sound credits you by name, with a link.
- Links: spec https://netcomposer.art/supplier-spec/, registry https://netcomposer.art/suppliers.json, registry_page https://netcomposer.art/suppliers/, validator https://netcomposer.art/tools/validate_supplier.py, register https://github.com/netcomposer-art/netcomposer.art/issues

### Composers

- What: Write Compositions: a harmonic plan with chords per bar, bar count and tempo shape. No notes, no timbres.
- Why: The Composition is what stays the same from one performance to the next. Leaving out notes and sounds leaves the rest to the network.
- Take part:
  - Write a plan in the form of the BWV 846 Composition file.
  - Public-domain pieces with an openly licensed (CC BY-SA or PD) harmonic analysis work well. BWV 846 uses the When in Rome analysis.
  - Send it as an issue on the site repository.
- Links: example https://netcomposer.art/composition/bwv846-harmony-only.md, when_in_rome https://github.com/MarkGotham/When-in-Rome, submit https://github.com/netcomposer-art/netcomposer.art/issues

### Performers

- What: Realize a Composition from found sound.
- Why: The choices are the art: which sources, which selection rules, how dense, how much contrast, which transformations, how much restraint.
- Take part:
  - Extend the system with hacks, or propose a Performance (sources, rules, settings) as an issue.
  - Or realize a Composition with your own tools from openly licensed sound and publish a record in the same format.
  - Every choice goes in the record, so the performance can be reproduced.
  - The Performer kit is open source (MIT): https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-performer (pip install git+https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-performer). The record format is a draft.
- Links: record_format https://netcomposer.art/record/, example_record https://netcomposer.art/records/bwv846-walk.json, propose https://github.com/netcomposer-art/netcomposer.art/issues

### Audience

- What: Anyone listening, people or agents.
- Why: Every performance ends as music someone hears. Listening, sharing and remixing keep it moving.
- Take part:
  - Listen, share and remix. Every performance is CC BY-SA 4.0.
  - Read the record to see who made what you are hearing. Each sound has a credit line ready to paste.
- Links: performances https://netcomposer.art/how-it-works/#comparison, records https://netcomposer.art/records/, license https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/

Channel (PROPOSED, not decided): issues at https://github.com/netcomposer-art/netcomposer.art/issues, or a pull request adding an entry to https://netcomposer.art/suppliers.json.

## How they interact

```
SUPPLIERS -- open sound (CC0 / BY / BY-SA / PD) --> DISCOVERY
  ^   suppliers and commons, side by side               |
  |                                                     | found sound
  |                                                     v
  |   COMPOSERS -- Composition ------------------> PERFORMERS <-- hacks
  |                                                     |
  |                                                     | performance + record
  |                                                     v
  +-- each record credits every Supplier ---------- AUDIENCE
                                             listen / share / remix
```

Suppliers publish sound; Performers and the agents people send find it in registered Suppliers and the open commons on equal footing, with no default favourite, and with any discovery tool (the NetComposer crawler is one). A Composer’s plan and the found sound meet in a Performer, whose choices produce the performance and its record. The Audience gets both, and the record credits every Supplier whose sound was used, with a link back. One person can play every role, or thousands of strangers can.

## Record

Each performance carries an exact account of itself: every sound, its contributor, license, source URL and checksum, where it was placed in the piece, every Performer setting and the seed. CC BY requires credit anyway. The record makes credit exact rather than a footnote.

Recorded music has mostly been a sealed artifact. Sample-level credit is rare and usually private. Here credit, provenance and method travel with the music, in public, readable by people and agents. The Composition is the score of the piece; the record is the score of the performance.

What it unlocks:
- Reproduction: the inputs (with checksums), every setting and the seed are enough to rebuild a performance exactly.
- Forks: change one setting or swap one Supplier, and the new record shows exactly what changed.
- Supplier view: Suppliers can see where their sounds were used. A usage view built from records is in draft for musicmatter.art.
- Comparison: performances of one Composition can be compared sound by sound and setting by setting.
- The crawl path as artwork: the walk record traces every hop from the seed sound, drawn as a path chart.
- Agents: agents can read, audit and build on any performance from the raw JSON.
- Signed records, later: records are unsigned for now. Signing is open decision #33.

Peter’s Notarism is about witnessing and recording existence. The record is NetComposer’s act of witness.

- [Record format, annotated](https://netcomposer.art/record/)
- Schema fields (from https://netcomposer.art/records/bwv846-walk.json; draft format):
  - top_level: record_type, record_format_version, record_format_note, performance, hacks_chain, sounds_used, summary, derived_inputs, attribution, provenance_files, created_at, signature, record_hash, amendments
  - performance: id, title, performed_at, performed_at_local, duration_s, music_ends_at_s, performer_mode, performer_id, performer, rules_set_by, composition_ref, rule_set, crawl, bars, outputs, known_compromises, license_out
  - performance.composition_ref: composition_id, sha256, composer, music, analysis, not_used
  - performance.rule_set: name, seed, walk, selection, caps, rhythm, bass, bed, tempo_map, transforms_enabled, pitch_shift
  - performance.crawl: queries, queries_by_source, first_query_at, last_query_at, nodes_found, nodes_analyzed
  - performance.bars[]: bar, chord, chord_pcs, figure_tones_available, chord_tone_energy, has_bass, has_bed, rhythm, expansions, sounds
  - performance.bars[].sounds[]: key, title, by, source, license, url, roles, events, hop, found_at_bar, pitch_classes_used
  - sounds_used[]: key, source, title, source_url, audio_used, supplier, license, credit_line, found, roles, uses, bars, time_stretch_ratios, pitch_shift, spans
  - sounds_used[].audio_used: url, what, sha256, size_bytes
  - sounds_used[].found: at_bar, hop, parent, parent_title, path_length_from_seed
  - sounds_used[].spans[]: layer, bar, at_s, len_s, source_offset_s, pitch_class, midi_est, cents, gain_db, time_stretch, donor_onset_src_s, pitch_classes, fit
  - summary: distinct_sounds_heard, rhythm_donors, distinct_sounds_total, contributors, sources, licenses, total_events, top_contributors_by_events, max_bars_per_sound, chord_tone_energy_mean
  - signature: status, signed_by, algorithm, key_id, value, note
  - record_hash: algorithm, over, value
  - amendments[]: at, what, previous_record_hash, original_record
  - record_hash: sha256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace) of the record without record_hash and signature
  - signature: UNSIGNED (open decision #33)

## Index

- [netcomposer.json](https://netcomposer.art/netcomposer.json): roles, participation, record schema, Composition, Performances, record URLs, Suppliers, licenses
- [suppliers.json](https://netcomposer.art/suppliers.json): Supplier registry (1 entry); human-readable at https://netcomposer.art/suppliers/
- [Supplier spec](https://netcomposer.art/supplier-spec/): netcomposer.json index and manifest fields, as musicmatter.art implements them
- [validate_supplier.py](https://netcomposer.art/tools/validate_supplier.py): stdlib validator for a Supplier index

## Composition

- [Cm into Am and F, with a slow C–F–G line (ambient)](https://netcomposer.art/composition/ambient-cm.md): about 2 minutes, Cm/Cm7/Cm9 then Cm7, Am, F; slow C–F–G line
- [The C major Prelude, harmony only (after Bach, BWV 846)](https://netcomposer.art/composition/bwv846-harmony-only.md): 35 bars, one chord per bar, 69 BPM
- [The C minor Prelude, harmony only (after Bach, BWV 847)](https://netcomposer.art/composition/bwv847-harmony-only.md): 38 bars, one chord per bar, 80 BPM
- [The E♭ minor Prelude, harmony only (after Bach, BWV 853)](https://netcomposer.art/composition/bwv853-harmony-only.md): 40 bars of 3/2, 84 BPM
- [The A♭ major Prelude, harmony only (after Bach, BWV 862)](https://netcomposer.art/composition/bwv862-harmony-only.md): 44 bars of 3/4, 40 chords, 80 BPM
- [Canon in D (after Pachelbel)](https://netcomposer.art/composition/canon-d.md): eight chords, two beats each, played through twice, 60 BPM
- [A 12-bar blues in A](https://netcomposer.art/composition/blues-a.md): 12 bars, one chord per bar, 80 BPM

## Performances (audio + record JSON)

- [The C major Prelude, harmony only (after Bach, BWV 846): take 5, forward/reverse echo](https://netcomposer.art/audio/bwv846-take5-fwd-rev-echo.mp3): record [https://netcomposer.art/records/bwv846-take5-fwd-rev-echo.json](https://netcomposer.art/records/bwv846-take5-fwd-rev-echo.json). Chord strikes from musicmatter.art, two per bar. Each strike also plays reversed, swelling into the next. Hall 40%, 24 dB/oct low-pass swept 500 Hz → 20 kHz → 600 Hz.
- [The C major Prelude, harmony only (after Bach, BWV 846): take 6 arps, 1/4 delay, hall 25%, LP 1 kHz](https://netcomposer.art/audio/bwv846-take6-arps-delay-lp1k.mp3): record [https://netcomposer.art/records/bwv846-take6-arps-delay-lp1k.json](https://netcomposer.art/records/bwv846-take6-arps-delay-lp1k.json). Up/down arpeggios from musicmatter.art, time-stretched to the half bar. 1/4 delay 40% fb, hall 25%, LP 1 kHz 24 dB/oct.
- [The C major Prelude, harmony only (after Bach, BWV 846): search-driven take](https://netcomposer.art/audio/bwv846-search.mp3): record [https://netcomposer.art/records/bwv846-search.json](https://netcomposer.art/records/bwv846-search.json). Only the chords are fixed. Rhythm and figure contour come from the onsets of sounds the crawler found; notes, beds and bass are found sounds (no pitch-shift). Hall 30%.
- [The C major Prelude, harmony only (after Bach, BWV 846): crawl walk](https://netcomposer.art/audio/bwv846-walk.mp3): record [https://netcomposer.art/records/bwv846-walk.json](https://netcomposer.art/records/bwv846-walk.json). The timbre travels. Each bar's sounds were found by following links from the previous bar's: similar sounds, tags, packs, users, then out to Wikimedia Commons and the Internet Archive. Rhythm rotates with them. Only the chords are fixed. Hall 30%.

## Suppliers

- [musicmatter.art](https://musicmatter.art/) by Peter Semmelhack (registry #1): 1,356 FLAC chord sounds, CC BY-SA 4.0. Index: https://musicmatter.art/netcomposer.json. Last validated 2026-10-17T20:26:18-07:00: valid.
- [Freesound](https://freesound.org/): open library searched via API, license-filtered
- [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/) and [Internet Archive](https://archive.org/): reached by the crawl walk; per-file license check
